text: Why is exactly-once delivery semantics actually hard in practice?
response: Instead of using algorithms to figure out when data is actually been sent, the semantics rely on the implementation always knowing when data is actually been sent.  This means the system does not need to figure out when data is actually been sent, as the implementation knows the data has been successfully acknowledged.  Therefore, the reliance on exactly-once delivery semantics is justified by the fact that the system never has to figure out when data is actually been sent.  Cite: RFC 9001 section 4.5.3
